findings.reason: the plan must name which recogniser survives and how the other is expressed over it, or the duplicate the section exists to remove survives its own repair.
findings.text: §18 speaks of "the constant and the landing-comment recogniser" (one of each) but the package carries two constants (`plan_review.RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX`, public, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:123`; `promotion._LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX`, private, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:7209`) and two recognisers of the same `startswith("c-run-")` rule (`plan_review._without_run_comments`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:329`; `promotion._landed_sections`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:7229`), plus an inline mint of the literal at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:3580`; §18's done-when only pins the literal to one module, so a worker satisfies the gate with both recognisers still alive importing one constant

findings.reason: §17 should either have the prose parser consume `plan_headings`' identities (the owner the section creates) or restate the exception's real reason, since the plan's current reason is contradicted one section earlier.
findings.text: §16 makes the prose parser record the enclosing section element and bucket its chunks by section identity, i.e. it enumerates sections, while §17 justifies keeping the prose parser's own h2 recognition (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:212`, reported as a permanent exception to the heading-walk rule) on the ground that "it enumerates no sections"; after §16 that justification is false, and section enumeration ends with two owners — `plan_headings` over the span parser and the prose parser's own bucket — kept in step only by §17's identity-equivalence test

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the public surface added across §16–§18 is a single reader, `plan_headings`, over one private parser, one private `_section_digests` map and the hoisted derivations; the identity derivation, span location, per-section digests and coverage predicate all sit behind it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 consolidates the landing-comment rule onto `reckon/_plan_html.py` but leaves two constants and two recognisers alive, and §16 grows a second section enumerator whose existence contradicts §17's stated reason for keeping a second h2 walk.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 adds exactly one public definition (`plan_headings`) and names the private walks it retires, §16 adds none and states why the identity digest and prose walk keep their names, §18 adds none, and no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is proposed by any of the three sections.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites machinery that exists and is the right one to extend: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94`), the AST census machinery `read_trees`/`definitions`/`_staged_writes` (`reckon/interface_counts.py:74,97`), `section_record_id` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:215`), and the four readers of the declaration map (`roadmap.implementable_sections`, `_schema.plan_executable_remainder`, `promotion._plan_remaining_sections`, `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `plan_headings` is the public face of a private parser consumed across five module boundaries and applies the hoisted identity at each heading; it is not a pass-through, and the plan says why the parser itself stays private.
